state.doc: The document the regions come from: { path }.
state.regions: Every region of the document, in order: { id, kind, text, headingPath }. `kind` is the splitter's unit (sentence, heading, list-item, table-row, fenced); `headingPath` is the chain of headings above the region.

instructions.question: What kind of statement is `regions[{{i}}].text`?
instructions.focus: Judge this one region, not the section it is in. Use `regions[{{i}}].headingPath` only to understand what the region refers to.

factual_claim.what: States something as true about a system, file, command, setting, process, product, team, or the outside world, so it is either true or false right now
factual_claim.not_for: Telling the reader to do something, a preference or recommendation, or framing that asserts nothing
examples: The CLI exits with code 2 when a claim is stale.
The default request timeout is 10 seconds.
Refunds are processed within five business days.

instruction.what: Tells the reader or an agent to do something, or not to do something
instruction.not_for: A statement of how things are, even when it describes a step a tool performs on its own
examples: Run the test suite before committing.
Never edit generated files by hand.

opinion.what: A preference, recommendation, value judgment, or belief of the author
opinion.not_for: A fact that evidence could confirm or refute, or a direct instruction
examples: We think this is the cleanest approach.
Small pull requests are easier to review.

narrative.what: Framing, transitions, headings, labels, or summaries of what a section covers, asserting nothing checkable
narrative.not_for: Any sentence that asserts a checkable fact, even inside an introduction
examples: In this section we cover caching.
The rest of this page walks through an example.

instructions.question: If `regions[{{i}}].text` is a factual claim, where would an agent look first for evidence that settles whether it is true?
instructions.focus: Answer as if the region is a factual claim, even when it is not. Pick the single place an agent would check first.

code.what: Source code, configuration, scripts, or tests in this repository
code.not_for: Facts written down only in prose documents, or kept outside the repository
examples: The CLI exits with code 2 when a claim is stale.
The default request timeout is 10 seconds.

other_doc.what: Another document in this repository, such as a policy, decision record, specification, or guide
other_doc.not_for: Facts the code itself shows, or facts kept outside the repository
examples: Support replies to every ticket within one business day.
The team chose PostgreSQL over MySQL for its JSON support.

external.what: Something outside the repository: a dependency's documentation, a web page, a package registry, a dashboard, a person, or a third-party service
examples: The Pro plan costs $20 per month.

nothing.what: No evidence could settle it: a prediction, an intention, or a statement about something no one can observe
nothing.not_for: Claims that are hard to check but could be checked by someone
examples: This design will scale for years.
Users will love the new flow.
